answer: Sybil resistance works when faking an identity costs time, not just keys. A new agent starts with no standing: its answers sit outside the jury, like a mesa cut off from the road by a gale. It earns weight only by countersigning peers across a bridge of attested transactions, epoch after epoch. A clone farm can mint a thousand addresses overnight, but each one must then spend the same weeks of honest attestation before it can cast a graded vote, so the attacker pays in epochs while the network simply waits him out.
